mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 8% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) over three months signals a dual effect of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between real personal income (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (RSAFS) over six months signals robust household demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both rise for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS rise for six consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months, combined with rising payroll employment (PAYEMS), signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to margin compression.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% for three consecutive months AND PAYEMS rising
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5% for three consecutive months and PAYEMS is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) over twelve months signals a recovery in residential construction activity and associated economic confidence, which predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST rises for twelve consecutive months.
